1.title: Granite: The Oldest Rock of the Vosges
1.html:
Granite is the oldest crystalline basement of the Vosges, and its weathering forms "granite sand" (arène granitique), sandy and extremely well-drained, rich in diverse minerals such as potassium, magnesium, fluorine and phosphorus — the key reason why wines from granite sites so often show delicate, multi-layered aromas.

Alsace has 8 granite Grand Crus, mostly concentrated around the Kaysersberg valley (Kientzheim, Katzenthal, Ammerschwihr, Niedermorschwihr, Turckheim) and in the north around Dambach-la-Ville, Blienschwiller, Kintzheim and Rodern.
2.title: Three Granite Representatives: The Kaysersberg Valley Group
2.items.0.label: Schlossberg (Kientzheim, 80.28 ha)
2.items.0.desc: The largest Grand Cru in Alsace! Migmatite plus intrusive Thannenkirch granite, rich in diverse minerals. The steep slope requires terraced farming. Mainly Riesling; from 1928 Kaysersberg / Kientzheim growers regulated the site's conditions through a written convention, later confirmed in the 1975 / 1992 decrees.
2.items.1.label: Sommerberg (Niedermorschwihr & Katzenthal, 28.36 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Turckheim two-mica granite, with slopes up to 45°! One of the steepest vineyards in all of Alsace. Planting recorded as early as 1214, and the "Sommerberg" boundary was already defined in the 17th century. Known for Riesling, which shows its full style after 1–3 years of ageing.
2.items.2.label: Wineck-Schlossberg (Katzenthal & Ammerschwihr, 27.40 ha)
2.items.2.desc: Also Turckheim two-mica granite, with the valley enclosing it on three sides to form a unique microclimate. Named after Wineck castle (the only castle in Alsace completely surrounded by vineyards). Riesling country, with good Gewurztraminer too.
3.question: What special status does Schlossberg (Kientzheim) have among the 51 Grand Crus?
3.options.0: It is the smallest Grand Cru
3.options.1: It is the largest Grand Cru (80.28 ha)
3.options.2: It is the only volcanic site
3.options.3: It is the only Grand Cru that allows blending
3.explanation: Schlossberg covers 80.28 hectares, the largest of the 51 Alsace Grand Crus, and is also a classic granite site whose production conditions were self-regulated by Kaysersberg and Kientzheim growers through a written convention as early as 1928, before the 1975 / 1992 decrees.
